verdict.rationale: Bitwarden documents an explicit API compatibility policy: it aims for indefinite backwards compatibility through semantic versioning and increments the major version when breaking changes are unavoidable. However, the versioning works at the release-cycle level, with no per-request version pinning (no version header or URL version). The evidence also shows no deprecation timelines, sunset notices, or migration windows. missing for 10: per-request API version pinning, a documented deprecation timeline/sunset process, independent corroboration of the policy in practice.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can rely on versioned APIs with a documented deprecation policy

citations.quote: As a practice, we aim to provide backwards compatibility to the API indefinitely through semantic versioning. However, if we add enhancements that make it difficult or impossible to maintain backwards compatibility to all prior versions, we will indicate that by incrementing the major version number.
